newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hopes Colombia drug move is just technical.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hopes Colombia drug move is just technical.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it hoped a Colombian decision to suspend aerial spraying of illicit drug crops had been taken for technical reasons and called for it to be resumed as soon as possible.
Colombia quietly suspended spraying operations on Wednesday in what was widely seen as a reprisal for a U.S. decision to leave the country on a drugs blacklist.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the decision came at a time when U.S. government estimates showed a 32 per cent increase in the cultivation of coca in Colombia, making it the second largest grower in the world.
Cocaine is made from the coca leaf.

"We've not received any explanation for this decision but believe me we have raised it with the Colombians today through our embassy (in Bogota), through ambassador (Myles) Frechette," Burns told reporters.
"We hope that this decision has been taken for technical reasons only and not policy reasons. And we certainly urge a resumption of eradication operations as soon as possible," Burns said.

There was no formal announcement of the suspension, which came just two days after Colombian Interior Minister Horacio Serpa denied that the government had any plans to retaliate against Washington's "decertification" of Colombia.

But Joaquin Polo, head of the National Drug Policy office, said in a radio interview that spraying had been temporarily suspended until the government had reviewed all its anti-drug agreements with the United States.
Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano, head of the National Police, said subsequently, however, that the suspension was to review the effectiveness of the programme.

Washington last Friday decertified Colombia for the second year running as an ally in the drug war. U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said the decision was taken because of "rampant corruption" at the highest levels of the Colombian government.
The move infuriated Colombian officials who warned that all bilateral cooperation agreements with the United States would be revised because of it.
